column2: skills/implement/scripts/oos-file-conflict-deps.sh:115-119,154-182 plan omits `clean_match` and pre-regex body normalization from the bash parity contract. scenario: the bash helper strips leading junk, trailing punctuation, embedded `./`, and splits `,`/`;` before `grep -eoh`. `python/research.py:extract_filelines` uses different boundary rules. a regex-only port can drop comma-adjacent paths (cases v/w) or mishandle dotfiles/makefile captures (cases l–n)

skills/implement/scripts/oos-file-conflict-deps.sh:276-291 plan does not pin one candidate edge per item pair with break after first conflicting shared path. scenario: bash records at most one `i\tj\tbasename` row per pair and unions once. emitting multiple rows per pair inflates `cluster_edges`, triggering chain degradation too early (case-j) or changing component shape

python/issue_create.py:150-206 plan does not state tsv indexes are `parse_issue_input` ordinals (1..len(items)), not `oos_n` heading numbers. scenario: case-t expects `1\t4` because a pending generic block becomes item 3 and `### oos_3` is item 4. indexing by heading number yields `1\t3` and breaks `/issue` intra-batch deps

python/file_oos.py:784-799 plan does not require env-cap validation before output cleanup registration. scenario: bash validates caps before the exit trap (lines 23–30). registering cleanup first and then exiting 2 on invalid caps can delete a pre-existing stable tsv on a path that should not publish

the plan routes `oos_filer` through the cli but copies `design_oos` degraded-continue semantics that treat exit-0 empty tsv like failure. per `skills/implement/references/oos-pipeline.md` step 3.5 and `skills/implement/references/execution-issues-tracking.md`, exit 0 + empty tsv should omit deps silently; non-zero exits (including global-cap exit 1 and invalid-cap exit 2) get the operator warning plus a `tool failures` entry. plan lines 77–80 bundle empty and non-zero and say to append the graceful-degrade warning for both.

the stale-reference sweep omits harness contract doc deletion. the `### updated: skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-file-conflict-deps.md` section is empty, but the file still literal-references `skills/implement/scripts/oos-file-conflict-deps.sh`. leaving it after the helper delete can fail `make lint-retired-scripts` despite the plan's acceptance gate. the harness contract file is neither deleted nor recorded with the retired harness: the plan adds retired-manifest rows for `oos-file-conflict-deps.sh` and `.md`, deletes `test-oos-file-conflict-deps.sh`, and leaves the test `.md` subsection empty. if the `.md` remains, `make lint-retired-scripts` will flag its exact retired helper path after the helper row is added; if it is deleted without manifest rows, the migrated harness is not recorded per the python migration recipe.

branch 3 runs `deps.unlink(missing_ok=true)` on every non-zero cli return, including exit `2`. that contradicts the env-cap preservation contract: `file_oos.py` exits `2` on invalid `oos_file_conflict_*` caps before output resolution and intentionally leaves any pre-existing stable tsv untouched. a same-tmpdir retry with bogus caps can delete a healthy `oos-intra-batch-deps.tsv` from an earlier success.

the plan deletes `skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-file-conflict-deps.sh` and `skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-file-conflict-deps.md`, but only records the helper `.sh`/`.md` in `migrated-scripts.tsv`. `make lint-retired-scripts` will not enforce absence of stale references to the retired harness/doc, so the harness migration is not fully verifiable under the repo migration contract.

the migration plan deletes `skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-file-conflict-deps.sh` and `skills/implement/scripts/test-oos-file-conflict-deps.md` but, per `docs/python-migration.md:49-54`, every retired bash script, harness, and `.md` sibling needs a `python/migrated-scripts.tsv` row so `make lint-retired-scripts` can catch stale references. `python/migrated-scripts.tsv` currently has no `oos-file-conflict` entries; only the helper `.sh`/`.md` rows are planned, leaving harness paths unregistered despite live references in `makefile`, `agent-lint.toml`, `docs/linting.md`, and `scripts/residual-bash-paths.txt`.

the plan’s `### updated: python/migrated-scripts.tsv` subsection (and related prose) requires retiring all four bash surfaces — helper `oos-file-conflict-deps.{sh,md}` plus harness `test-oos-file-conflict-deps.{sh,md}` — but the enumerated manifest rows cover only the helper pair. if the implementer deletes all four files but registers only two rows, `make lint-retired-scripts` will not enforce harness literals still referenced in `makefile`, `agent-lint.toml`, `docs/linting.md`, and `scripts/residual-bash-paths.txt`, so migration can appear clean while stale harness references remain unguarded.
